material.notes: Five M3 variants (filled, tonal, elevated, outlined, text) in enabled, hovered, focused, pressed, disabled; button_icon.png adds the 18 dp leading icon (16 dp start, 24 dp end, 8 dp gap); fab.png has the small (40, r12), regular (56, r16), large (96, r28) and extended FABs and the four icon buttons (40 dp circle in a 48 dp target). Exact spec values: 40 dp height, full corners, 24 dp side padding, state layers 8/10/10 %, disabled 12 % container / 38 % label, outlined focus outline turns primary, M3 baseline colours, Roboto Medium 14/20 labels. Approximations: elevated shadow, text-button padding with an icon (16 where M3 says 12).
gaps: The icon-button toggled forms are approximated (standard primary icon; filled primary; tonal secondary-container; outlined inverse-surface)
The elevated button's tonal surface tint at hover (elevation 2) is the 8 % layer only
Evidence is the published Material 3 spec geometry from memory, not a capture of a device: nothing here was measured against an Android screenshot
Elevation is the Neper shadow (a hard offset, no blur) and no surface tint is drawn; the M3 tonal surface colours stand in for tint
No letter spacing: the M3 type scale tracks its text (label-large 0.1 sp, body-medium 0.25 sp, body-large 0.5 sp), the text layout cannot
No ripple: pressed is the 10 % state layer only (Android adds a ripple on top)
Icons are Neper's stroked glyphs, not Material Symbols (a settings gear, an alert circle and a person differ in drawing)
